content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a comprehensive framework for creating evidence-based immunization policies and strategic guidance. This process is led by the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), which is tasked with providing recommendations based on high-quality, contemporary data. These recommendations are developed using internationally recognized methodologies and best practices. SAGE is the principal advisory group to WHO on all vaccine and immunization-related matters. It advises on global policies and strategies, covering the entire spectrum of immunization activities, from research and development to implementation and delivery. SAGE consists of at least 15 internationally renowned experts in immunization and related fields, selected through an open nomination process. Members serve in a personal, voluntary capacity and are not representatives of any government or organization. They are required to disclose any potential conflicts of interest, and their work is guided by WHO’s rules on transparency and integrity. SAGE recommendations are based on a thorough assessment of the benefits and risks of vaccines, as well as contextual factors such as feasibility, acceptability, disease prevalence, equity, gender considerations, and cost-effectiveness. These recommendations typically apply to a class of vaccines with similar characteristics and performance profiles. In rare cases, SAGE addresses product-specific issues, particularly during public health emergencies of international concern (PHEICs) when rapid policy advice is needed. SAGE is supported by working groups, which are temporary advisory groups established to conduct in-depth reviews of specific topics. The working groups prepare independent evaluations of scientific and technical evidence, which are then used by SAGE to develop final recommendations. The SAGE Secretariat, based at WHO headquarters in Geneva, provides administrative and technical support to SAGE and its working groups. The Secretariat monitors the global vaccine landscape, tracks data from vaccine monitoring systems, and collects requests for SAGE advice. These requests are assessed for their suitability, and topics are prioritized based on WHO’s strategic goals and resources. SAGE meetings are held biannually and include both open and closed sessions. Open sessions allow for the exchange of non-confidential information, while closed sessions are used to finalize recommendations. Decisions are reached by consensus, and in cases where consensus cannot be achieved, additional information is sought, or minority opinions are documented. In exceptional circumstances, such as health emergencies, extraordinary meetings may be convened to provide immediate guidance. Following SAGE meetings, the group’s recommendations are presented to the WHO Director-General for approval before being publicly communicated. These recommendations are advisory, and WHO retains full control over subsequent decisions. All SAGE-related materials, including meeting agendas, reports, and vaccine position papers, are made publicly available on the WHO SAGE website. Final decisions regarding conflicts of interest are made by WHO to maintain the highest standards of integrity in its activities.
